comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C1, C26-C34, C36-C38, C41-C42) about NuRD asymmetric distribution. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging data from live imaging, timing, and quantitative measurements. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, raising critical concerns that NuRD asymmetry may simply result from daughter cell size asymmetry rather than active segregation, and criticizing lack of appropriate controls to distinguish active from passive mechanisms.

Both evaluate claims C44-C45 about PIG-1 dependency of NuRD asymmetry. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on fluorescence imaging in pig-1 mutants. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with the editor noting the model is 'supported by solid data' and no specific concerns raised about PIG-1 experiments, though this does not resolve broader mechanism questions.

Both evaluate claims C4-C5, C68-C70 about NuRD-V-ATPase physical interaction. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on biochemical evidence identifying 12 V-ATPase subunits and western blot confirmation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the evidence is 'rather weak' and criticizing lack of appropriate negative controls (ACT-4::GFP or GFP alone) for the co-IP experiment.

Both evaluate claims about NuRD sufficiency for cell survival (C3, C78-C84). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on BafA1 treatment and auxin-inducible degradation showing causal role. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting BafA1 causes 'pleiotropic effects' visible in Figure 5E and that critical evidence for specificity was not shown, raising doubt about whether survival is specifically due to ectopic NuRD.

Both evaluate pH asymmetry claims (C7, C73-C74, C76-C77). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on pHluorin imaging, noting the caveat about protein amount changes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating that 'symmetric inheritance of GFP and mCherry is not appropriate evidence to estimate the level of pHluorin' and that this issue 'remains unsolved,' questioning whether pH measurements accurately reflect true pH differences.

Both evaluate the mechanistic link between NuRD and egl-1 regulation (C2, C56-C67). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on transcriptional upregulation, promoter activity, and chromatin changes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating authors 'do not provide evidence' that effects are not due to 'global effects on development' and that 'no causal interactions have been demonstrated,' noting pleiotropic developmental defects in Figure S7B.

Both evaluate V-ATPase asymmetric distribution (C6, C85-C86, with peer also considering C87-C88). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on live imaging showing co-segregation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing concerns about BafA1 pleiotropic effects, lack of appropriate controls, and unresolved questions about whether asymmetry reflects active segregation versus cell size differences.

OpenEval R3 evaluates systematic embryonic lineage analysis (C46-C47, C52) and rates SUPPORTED. Peer R7 evaluates overlapping claims (C46-C52) but rates UNCERTAIN, citing confusion about error bars in Figure 2B, requesting data in table format for verification, and noting issues with 'inappropriate graphs' and 'error bars disconnected,' creating uncertainty about statistical robustness.

OpenEval R4 evaluates exceptions to NuRD-apoptosis relationship (C48-C51) and rates SUPPORTED. Peer R7 includes these claims in broader lineage analysis (C46-C52) rated UNCERTAIN due to data presentation and statistical concerns, though the specific exception findings are not directly contested.

OpenEval R11 evaluates loss of NuRD and V-ATPase asymmetry with BafA1 (C8, C78, C87-C88) and rates SUPPORTED with caution about pleiotropic effects. Peer R6 evaluates pH asymmetry (C7-C8, C73-C74, C76-C77) and rates UNCERTAIN, with concerns about pHluorin controls that also apply to BafA1 experiments, though only partial claim overlap.

Both evaluate the proposed mechanistic model. OpenEval R12 (C89, C93-C95) rates UNCERTAIN, noting pH's causal role in segregation is speculative. Peer R9 (C9-C10, C90, C92-C95) also rates UNCERTAIN, with editor noting 'disagreement remained' and that 'alternative possibilities' were incorporated, with multiple unresolved concerns undermining the specific molecular mechanism.

OpenEval R14 evaluates the overall mechanistic model (C90, C92) and rates SUPPORTED while noting the causal chain is inferred rather than directly demonstrated. Peer R9 evaluates overlapping mechanistic claims (C9-C10, C90, C92-C95) and rates UNCERTAIN due to multiple unresolved methodological concerns about controls, pleiotropic effects, and causal relationships.

OpenEval R5 evaluates apoptosis assays and genetic epistasis (C2, C53-C59) and rates SUPPORTED. Peer R2 evaluates broader mechanistic claims including some overlap (C2, C56-C59 plus C60-C67) and rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about global developmental effects rather than specific causal interactions.
OpenEval R13 evaluates ER colocalization (C103-C104) and rates SUPPORTED, noting the cargo delivery inference is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval R15 evaluates limitations of scRNA-seq data interpretation (C96-C99) and rates SUPPORTED as appropriate scientific caution. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological limitation claims.

OpenEval R16 evaluates mechanistic hypotheses about differential asymmetry (C106-C107, C109, C111) and rates UNCERTAIN, noting proposals are speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic speculation claims.

OpenEval R17 evaluates rare NuRD asymmetry in non-apoptotic divisions (C115-C117) and rates SUPPORTED for observations but notes broader role inference is speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval R18 evaluates background knowledge claims (C11-C25) and rates SUPPORTED as well-established context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not evaluate background literature claims.
OpenEval R19 evaluates additional background knowledge (C71-C72, C75, C91) and rates SUPPORTED as well-established context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval R20 evaluates knowledge gap characterization (C100-C101) and rates SUPPORTED as appropriate positioning of novelty. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these framing claims.
